cases.description: Header returns rcode 0 and no OPT record is present; method should return 0.
Header returns rcode 3 and no OPT record is present; method should return 3.
Header returns rcode 0, OPT record is present with extendedRcode 1; 1 << 4 = 16, so result should be 16.
Header returns rcode 2, OPT record is present with extendedRcode 5; 5 << 4 = 80, 80 + 2 = 82.
Header returns rcode 15, OPT record is present with extendedRcode 15; 15 << 4 = 240, 240 + 15 = 255.
Header returns rcode 20, OPT record is present with extendedRcode 20; 20 << 4 = 320, 320 + 20 = 340.
Header returns a negative rcode (-5) and no OPT record; method should simply return -5 (branch where opt is null).
OPT record is present but its extended rcode is 0; the method should return the header rcode unchanged (7).
Maximum 8‑bit values for both header rcode and extended rcode. 255 + (255 << 4) = 255 + 4080 = 4335.
Header returns a negative rcode while an OPT record adds a positive extended rcode. Result = -3 + (2 << 4) = -3 + 32 = 29.
Integer overflow case: Integer.MAX_VALUE (2,147,483,647) plus (1 << 4) wraps around to -2,147,483,633 according to two's‑complement arithmetic.
Extended rcode is negative (simulating a malformed OPT record). Calculation: 10 + ((-1) << 4) = 10 + (-16) = -6.
Header field is null; calling getRcode() should throw NullPointerException when attempting header.getRcode().
OPT record is present but its getExtendedRcode() method throws an IllegalStateException; the exception should propagate out of getRcode().
